newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Communists threaten not to join Socialists.
newsitem.headline: French Communists threaten not to join Socialists.

text.p: France's Communist Party said on Thursday it may support a left-wing government without joining it should the left win Sunday's parliamentary election.

Alain Bocquet, president of the Communist group in the outgoing National Assembly, told a leftist rally in the northern city of Lille the Communists would be loyal to a leftist government, "whether we participate in a government or whether we support it without participating."
That raised the prospect of the Communists seeking no ministers in a leftist cabinet.
Bocquet said that should the left win Sunday's vote, a decision would be made by the party at a mass meeting on Monday

The Communists had previously taken a similar stance towards a leftist government in 1984, supporting it while withdrawing its ministers from the cabinet and denouncing a Socialist "turn to the right".

The prospect of both Communist and Socialist ministers in a leftist government, sharing power with conservative President Jacques Chirac, has been a major target of centre-right politicians in the election campaign.
Critics in the governing centre-right have said such a cabinet would be divided and thus incapable of dealing with France's problems should the left win power.
For example, they note, the Communist Party opposes European monetary union while the Socialists generally favour it.

Some analysts speculate that the left, which won an upset victory over the current majority in last Sunday's first-round vote, might win enough seats in next Sunday's runoff to have a majority of the seats in the National Assembly without help from the Communists.
But Bocquet's statement could also signal that hardline Communists have been arguing that their party should not join a Socialist-dominated government because it would compromise their goals.
